text:
Devon: Quick thread — I'm exploring a control-plane split pattern for Private customers: tiny local CP in-customer-vpc that handles auth/handshake + egress orchestration, while global CP keeps global policies and billing. main question: how do we manage tenant-egress orchestration and cutovers without breaking source-ip preservation?
Maria: +1 to separation for blast radius. concern: cert propagation/windowing during cutover. we saw 30s spikes during last peering flip.
Alex: Can we do staged cutover: route-level canary where a percentage of traffic goes to local cp egress first? if local cp fails, fallback to global cp. That preserves continuity.
Sam: Important: the egress orchestrator must own ephemeral IP leases and NAT mapping. otherwise we lose SRC IP. Also need ttl for leases to avoid IP thrash.
Priya: Ops question — do we require a control-plane sidecar in each tenant subnet to maintain BGP/route state? or can we use a lightweight agent + managed relay? sidecar increases ops but simplifies cutover.
Devon: Thinking lightweight agent that requests 2-phase lease: PREPARE -> ACTIVATE. PREPARE allocates IP and fetches certs but not inserted into dataplane. ACTIVATE flips routing. That lets us test certs before changing paths.
Alex: Love PREPARE/ACTIVATE. add a REVOCATION step for rollback. Also we should emit probe metrics before ACTIVATE: tcp connect to well-known endpoint, small request latency.
Maria: Note on certs: use short-lived certs (5m) for the local handshake so rotation is cheap. but need monotonic sequence numbers so older certs can't be replayed.
Sam: For source-ip preservation: if we advertise from local cp, ensure we preserve ARP/ENI ownership. option A: attach ENI per-tenant (costly). option B: SNAT with consistent mapping table. prefer B if we can keep mapping sticky.
Priya: SNAT mapping table needs persistence across failovers. flush on cutover leads to 502 burst. can we backfill mapping to fallback path?
Devon: Proposal: orchestrator replicates mapping to both global cp and local cp during PREPARE. only ACTIVATE changes dataplane pointer. replication done via compact changelog (per-tenant) to avoid large writes.
Alex: Implementation sketch: 
```
# PREPARE
POST /v1/tenants/123/egress/leases { "cidr": "/32", "mode": "dual-write" }
# ACTIVATE
POST /v1/tenants/123/egress/leases/activate { "lease_id": "abc" }
```
Priya: Observability: tracer spans must include lease_id, cert_seq, and route_version. add dashboard for "pre-activate probe failures" and "activate rollback rate".
Maria: Rollout plan: 1) enable PREPARE/dual-write for 5% tenants; 2) monitor mapping replication lag and probe success; 3) enable ACTIVATE for that cohort; 4) widen. keep fallback to global cp for 24h after activation.
Sam: Edge-case: brief divergent mappings between local and global => traffic split can cause stuck TCP sessions. mitigation: grace window where both sides respond to same IPs for N seconds using conntrack sync. can we push conntrack export?
Devon: conntrack export across accounts is hard. alternative: short-lived flow-handoff: set tcp-mgr to politely RST old path after handoff window. reduce connection thrash.
Alex: Security: ensure local cp only has scoped KMS access. restrict signing keys to ephemeral keywrap. audit logs sent to global CP.
Priya: Automation: operator CLI: `rictl tenant-egress prepare` / `activate` with dry-run to show diffs. include `--simulate-path` to run probes.
Devon: Draft TODOs:
- spec PREPARE/ACTIVATE API (openapi snippet)
- implement dual-write replication w/ changelog and idempotency keys
- add probe suite and dashboards
- cutover playbook with rollback steps and SLO targets
- cost model: ENI vs SNAT sticky table vs dual-write complexity
Maria: Anyone up for a quick spike this week to validate replication lag with a fake mapping load? I can pair with Sam.
Sam: I can do it. will create a small harness that writes 10k mappings and measures tail latency.
infra-bot: Deploy job queued: egress-spike-harness-runner (job id: job-8772).
Devon: Great — @Maria @Sam do a short writeup once you have numbers. we'll sync tomorrow 9am PT in arch sync. :thumbsup:
Priya: Added a checklist item for 'cert monotonicity test' to the doc.
Alex: One last note: ensure canary tenants are low-risk (not enterprise financial). label tenants with `egress-canary=true` to auto-qualify.
Devon: Thanks all — this thread will become the followup RFC section. I'll capture the PREPARE/ACTIVATE state machine and post an RFC draft by EOD.
